extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal funds (K-12 and postsecondary educational institutions), Title IX Coordinators, and institutional administrators implementing Title IX compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on implementing §106.44 (now titled “Barriers to Reporting”) including the Title IX Coordinator's duty to monitor for and address barriers to reporting sex discrimination and the notification requirements for employees. Focused on what recipients must do and examples of appropriate, permissible, and impermissible actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator must monitor for barriers to reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.44(b) requires the recipient to require its Title IX Coordinator to monitor the recipient's education program or activity for barriers to reporting information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX (now framed as “Barriers to Reporting”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of barriers include inaccessible complaint reporting processes, confusing or non‑transparent grievance procedures, difficult‑to‑reach Title IX Coordinators or staff who discourage reporting, delays or perceptions of bias, and obstacles affecting students with disabilities or limited English proficiency. The Department clarified the obligation is focused specifically on barriers to reporting, not on monitoring all conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take steps reasonably calculated to address identified barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient becomes aware of a barrier to reporting sex discrimination, the Title IX Coordinator must take steps that are reasonably calculated to address that barrier, tailored to the specific impediments identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible responses include targeted trainings (departmental or staff-specific), widespread training for staff and students, more frequent/prominent publication of the Title IX Coordinator's contact information, relocating the Coordinator's office for visibility and accessibility, providing adequate staff for the Coordinator's office, enhanced training to avoid conflicts of interest and to prevent discouraging reporting, and developing user‑friendly Title IX materials. The obligation is ongoing and responses should reflect the facts and context of the recipient's educational environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in methods; no mandated specific monitoring steps
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to mandate particular methods (e.g., requiring campus climate surveys) or specific actions to monitor for or address barriers to reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have flexibility to choose strategies appropriate to their setting and resources. While recipients may use campus surveys or other tools, the Department will not require them; similarly, the Department declined to require elementary and secondary schools to educate students on healthy relationships. Recipients should tailor efforts to be effective in their context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limited to conduct that 'reasonably' may constitute sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The final text clarifies that monitoring and notification obligations apply to information about conduct that 'reasonably' may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or 'this part' (i.e., as defined in the regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrows the scope from speculative or purely hypothetical conduct and addresses concerns about diverting resources from meritorious complaints. Employees need not have definitive proof; information that could reasonably be understood to constitute sex discrimination (including sex‑based harassment) triggers the notification duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring does not require surveillance of academic discourse or students' online activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are not expected or required to monitor students' online activity, social media, or classroom academic discourse as part of §106.44(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX enforcement must be interpreted consistent with First Amendment protections and academic freedom. If speech (including classroom comments) nonetheless creates a barrier to reporting, recipients must address the barrier in ways that do not infringe protected speech (for example, by clarifying reporting policies rather than censoring viewpoint‑based speech).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements for employees (§106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must require employees (other than confidential employees) to either notify the Title IX Coordinator of information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination or, as applicable, provide the Title IX Coordinator's contact information and information on how to make a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At elementary and secondary schools, all non‑confidential employees must notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination. At postsecondary institutions, employees who do not have authority to institute corrective action or administrative leadership, teaching, or advising responsibility may be required either to notify or to provide contact/complaint information to the reporting party. The final rule streamlines and clarifies these requirements by dividing §106.44(c) into subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employees' reporting standard and training obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees are required to act on information about conduct that 'reasonably' may constitute sex discrimination; they are not required to make a final determination that sex discrimination occurred before reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under §106.8(d)(1), recipients must train all employees on the scope of conduct that constitutes sex discrimination (including sex‑based harassment) so employees can recognize reportable information. If an employee directly witnesses conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, the employee is deemed to have 'information' and must report or provide contact info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employees and required disclosures about reporting duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential employees are not subject to the mandatory notification duties that apply to non‑confidential employees, but the Department modified §106.44(d)(2) to require a confidential employee to explain to an informant the circumstances in which the confidential employee is not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may make confidential employees available to provide confidential support without notification obligations. The Department declined to require posting of reporting protocols online but requires recipients to include reporting information in the notice of nondiscrimination under §106.8(c)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for personally identifiable information (PII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.44(j) prohibits disclosure of personally identifiable information obtained in the course of complying with this part, except in limited, specified circumstances (e.g., to authorized legal representatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must safeguard PII obtained under notification obligations and comply with the limits on disclosure set out in §106.44(j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibility, delegation, and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The compliance obligation rests with the recipient, which must require the Title IX Coordinator to perform the monitoring and response duties; the Title IX Coordinator may delegate specific duties but must retain ultimate oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a recipient fails to ensure its Title IX Coordinator complies with the duty to monitor and address barriers, the recipient may be subject to administrative enforcement actions and will be given notice and an opportunity to come into compliance. The Department will provide technical assistance as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may not avoid Title IX duties by routing reports externally
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient cannot avoid compliance with §106.44(c) by requiring reporting to an external third party; the Title IX Coordinator must still ensure reports reach the Coordinator and must exercise oversight over delegated responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where an external entity receives reports, the recipient retains responsibility to ensure reporting obligations under Title IX are fulfilled consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: No mandated requirement to follow up with reporters to check for retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined commenters' requests to mandate follow‑up with individuals who report sex discrimination to ensure they are not experiencing further discrimination or retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because additional discrimination and retaliation are prohibited by other provisions of the regulations (including §§106.44 and 106.71), the Department left follow‑up practices to recipients' discretion; recipients may choose to follow up where factually warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with State and local laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in these final regulations precludes recipients from complying with state or local laws that also require notification to supervisors or others, provided there is no conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a conflict between Title IX obligations and state/local law exists, the recipient's Title IX obligations remain; whether a conflict exists must be determined based on the facts and the specific state/local requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing nature of obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's obligation to monitor for and take steps reasonably calculated to address barriers to reporting is ongoing, not a one‑time duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should build continuous monitoring and remediation into their Title IX compliance programs so they can promptly and effectively identify and address barriers as they arise.
